$comment: The actions Tiehall records a security event for, mirroring the list of activity-log: Which actions are security events, one item per bullet of the spec, in its order. Each action names the task that builds it until that task does; then it names the type of its security event and the test that shows the action appending that event together with its change (a test file of the repository and the exact title of a test in it). pnpm check:security-events checks this file.

items.item: a sign-in, and a refused sign-in, naming the GitHub account that was refused; a sign-in that clears an admin removal's block, as the sign-in capability defines, SHALL name the clearing;

actions.action: a sign-in

test.case: appends a security event naming the user, right after the session is stored, with the client's address and user agent kept apart

actions.action: a refused sign-in

test.case: appends a security event naming the GitHub account that was refused, and creates no session or user

actions.action: a sign-in that admits a new member, who joins with it

test.case: signs in, joins the install as a member, and the join and the sign-in are security events

actions.action: a sign-in that clears an admin removal's block

test.case: is admitted by an invite created after the removal, which clears the block, and the sign-in's security events name the clearing

items.item: a role change, an invite, the revocation of an invite, and a member's removal, naming whether an admin removed them, with the block that such a removal records, or they were removed because they left the GitHub organization, as the sign-in capability defines;

actions.action: a role change

test.case: makes the member an admin, and the activity log gains a security event naming the admin, the member and the new role

actions.action: an invite

test.case: is bound to the GitHub account the username names, with the role member, expires 7 days after it is created, and is a security event

actions.action: the revocation of an invite

test.case: needs no confirmation step: the revoked invite admits no one, and the activity log holds a security event for the revocation

actions.action: the revocation of an invite that a new one replaces

test.case: revokes the pending invite in the same write, records both, lists one invite, and the sign-in accepts the new one with its role

actions.action: a member's removal by an admin, with the block it records

test.case: ends the membership of the install and of every team, and records a security event naming the admin and the block

actions.action: a member's removal because they left the GitHub organization

test.case: catches a change no event reported, in polling mode, and records it as the system's

items.item: a person added to a team or removed from a team, naming the admin, the person and the team;

actions.action: a person added to a team

test.case: adding a person is a security event naming the admin, the person and the team, with no confirmation step, and adding them again records nothing

actions.action: a person removed from a team

test.case: removing a person is a security event naming the admin, the person and the team, and removing them again records nothing

items.item: a change of the sign-in policy;

actions.action: a change of the sign-in policy

test.case: to invited people only applies once confirmed, removes no member, and is a security event naming the admin and both settings

items.item: an agent client's approval, and the revocation of an agent grant;

actions.action: an agent client's approval

test.case: is a security event naming the member and the client, with the address and user agent kept apart

actions.action: the revocation of an agent grant

test.case: is a security event, removes the grant and stops its refresh token at once

items.item: a personal access token created or revoked;

actions.action: a personal access token created

test.case: records a security event that names the member and the token, never the value

actions.action: a personal access token revoked

test.case: makes its next call get 401 at once, is a security event, and leaves the page

items.item: an integration connected, changed or disconnected, and a new private key uploaded for the install's GitHub App;

actions.action: a GitHub installation connected

test.case: connects it once an admin confirms it: its repositories are read at once and count as covered, and a security event records it

actions.action: a GitHub installation disconnected

test.case: needs no confirmation step: it stops covering the repositories, keeps every member, and is a security event

actions.action: GitHub's mode switched by an admin

test.case: switches GitHub between the modes in the web UI, each switch a security event naming the admin

actions.action: GitHub put in polling mode by a failed delivery in the App's delivery log

test.case: puts GitHub in polling mode on a failed delivery after the first installation, which the admin page shows and the activity log records

actions.action: GitHub put in polling mode by a given-up delivery

test.case: is given up once it still fails after the fifth request: in one write the App's row records it and GitHub moves to polling mode, which the admin page shows, with a security event that names no user

actions.action: GitHub put in polling mode by a removed webhook

test.case: moves GitHub to polling mode, even after an admin's switch to webhook mode, with a security event that names no user, the webhook banner and one email

actions.action: the GitHub App's webhook secret stored

test.case: stores the secret encrypted once an admin confirms it, replacing any stored one, and records a security event for the changed integration

actions.action: the install's GitHub App replaced by a new App in a step that setup reopen opened, whose installations it disconnects

test.case: with a new App: deletes the old App's credentials, disconnects its installations, connects only the new App's when an admin closes it, and keeps members, teams, roles, grants and tokens

actions.action: the Jira connection connected
the Jira connection changed
the Jira connection disconnected
a new private key uploaded for the install's GitHub App

test.case: checks a valid key with GET /app under a JWT signed with it and issued by the stored client id, requests no installation token, stores it encrypted, uses it for the next call, and records a security event

items.item: an Atlassian account linked or unlinked by its user, and an admin's removal of a link, as the tracker-mirrors capability defines;

actions.action: an Atlassian account linked by its user
an Atlassian account unlinked by its user
an admin's removal of an Atlassian link

items.item: an API registered for contract reports, and an API unregistered;

actions.action: an API registered for contract reports

test.case: registers it once an admin confirms it on its review page, bound to the repository's GitHub ids, and records a security event

actions.action: an API unregistered

test.case: needs no confirmation step: an admin's form on the APIs page unregisters it, and a security event records it

actions.action: a contract-change fan-out confirmed

test.case: opens the last 2 once an admin confirms it with the confirmation step, which is a security event, and its banner goes

items.item: a change to the PAT switch, the longest PAT lifetime or the daily write budget;

actions.action: a change to the PAT switch

test.case: switched off by an admin with the confirmation step makes every existing PAT get 403, and switched on again restores unexpired ones

actions.action: a change to the longest PAT lifetime

test.case: set shorter by an admin with the confirmation step applies to new PATs, and is a security event

actions.action: a change to the daily write budget

test.case: is an admin's action with the confirmation step: a confirmed change to 8,000 applies and is a security event

items.item: an operator command run on the host, `admin grant` or `setup reopen`, as the self-host-install capability defines, naming the command and what it changed, and no user;

actions.action: admin grant run on the host, making a member an admin

test.case: makes the member whose login is given an admin, recorded as a security event member.role_changed that names the command and no user

actions.action: admin grant run on the host, changing nothing

test.case: changes nothing for a login that belongs to no member and says so, recording the run as a security event operator.command_run that names the command and no user

actions.action: setup reopen run on the host

test.case: prints a new setup code, records a security event naming the command and no user, and the install keeps serving members, sessions and tokens with the App in use

items.item: a `reconciled` event, as the requirement on reconciliation defines;

actions.action: a reconciled event

test.case: a role change stored while its event was dropped gains a reconciled event naming the member and the role they hold now

items.item: an export of the activity log;

actions.action: an export of the activity log

test.case: gives Pia a JSONL file with one event per line, including the role change and the claim, and the activity log then holds a security event for the export that names Pia

items.item: the completion of setup, naming the first admin.

actions.action: the completion of setup

test.case: makes the person the first admin, connects every installation the listing holds, and records the completion naming them
